subject: POC Trial Environment: Hosted vs Dedicated Sandbox vs VPC - Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan@acmeai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: POC Trial Environment: Hosted vs Dedicated Sandbox vs VPC - Next Steps

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion on the integration patterns and your evaluation goals. I wanted to recap the success criteria we agreed on and propose a concrete POC plan so we can get you started next week.

Success criteria (from our call):
- Endpoint latency under 250ms p50 for conversational flows (sample traffic attached)
- Token cost below $0.0008/token for batch scoring workloads
- Reproducible behavior across user dataset (no PII leakage; deterministic prompts for evaluation set)
- Deployment option that meets security: either hosted isolated sandbox or VPC with customer-managed networking

Evaluation plan / recommended approach:
1) Kickoff (1 day): introduce infra and provide test dataset + evaluation prompts.
2) Week 1 — Hosted trial (preferred fast path): we provide a hosted trial environment pre-configured with your evaluation model and sample KV cache settings. This gets you immediate telemetry (latency, tokens, quality) with minimal setup.
3) Week 2 — Performance test: if you need dedicated throughput, we spin up a temporary Dedicated Sandbox (reserved GPU pool) for 48–72 hours to run peak-load tests.
4) Week 3 — VPC trial (optional): if you require customer-managed networking and KMS, we provision a VPC trial environment. Note: provisioning can take 5–10 business days depending on your network approvals.

Ownership / next steps:
- Redwood: Rafael (technical onboarding) + Nikhil (commercial/contracting)
- Acme AI: Jordan (product owner) + Lina (infra lead)

Actions I propose now:
- Jordan: confirm which trial path you want to prioritize (hosted first vs request VPC straight away)
- Lina: share any network constraints (eg IP allowlist windows, egress/ingress rules)
- I will attach two documents: poc-environment-options.pdf (environment pros/cons + timelines) and mvp-success-criteria.xlsx (evaluation set + metrics).

If you’re happy, I’ll book a 30-minute kickoff for Monday 9/20 with Rafael to get credentials and payloads.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: poc-environment-options.pdf, mvp-success-criteria.xlsx
From: Jordan Price <jordan@acmeai.com>

Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC Trial Environment: Hosted vs Dedicated Sandbox vs VPC - Next Steps

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. Quick clarifying questions: 

1) For the hosted trial you suggest in Week 1, will our test data be uploaded to Redwood? We need clarity on data residency and whether sample data stays in your environment or is routed through our VPC.
2) For the Dedicated Sandbox, what kind of GPUs and concurrency should we expect during the 48–72h window? Need to know if that will match our prod-like load.
3) Lina: any blockers on our side for the VPC timeline — I’ve looped you in. If a network approval will take >5 business days, we may prefer hosted first.

Also can you share a ballpark cost delta between hosted trial (metered) vs Dedicated Sandbox (daily reserved cost) so I can prep procurement? I’ll also add Procurement (procurement@acmeai.com) if we need to discuss terms.

-Jordan
Product Lead | Acme AI
jordan@acmeai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan@acmeai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>, Lina Gomez <lina@acmeai.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Trial Environment: Hosted vs Dedicated Sandbox vs VPC - Next Steps

Jordan — great questions. Answers below inline.

1) Data residency for Hosted trial: your evaluation dataset will be stored in Redwood's hosted environment for the duration of the trial and will be deleted at the end of the engagement unless you request otherwise. We can enable encryption-at-rest and limit access to the trial tenant. If you need the data to never leave your VPC, we should start with the VPC trial.

2) Dedicated Sandbox spec: typical setup for a 48–72h perf run is 4x A100/80GB-equivalent GPUs with a concurrency layer that simulates your target throughput (we'll run the exact traffic pattern from your sample). If you need a different SKU we can accommodate but provisioning lead time is ~48 hours once authorized.

3) Cost delta (rough): Hosted trial (metered): estimated $300–$600 for a full week of evaluation depending on token volume. Dedicated Sandbox (48–72h reservation): $4,500 flat for the reserved window (includes GPU reservation and engineering support). VPC trial: pricing varies (additional engineering + network setup) — Rafael will follow up with a firm estimate once we know your network model.

Next steps I propose: Rafael will own technical onboarding and will schedule the hosted tenant credentials if you’re ok to start there. Nikhil will loop in procurement if you want the dedicated window authorized.

Jordan, can you confirm: (A) hosted-first ok? (B) preferred kickoff times Monday 9/20 morning PST or afternoon PST?

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: POC Trial Environment: Hosted vs Dedicated Sandbox vs VPC - Next Steps

Looping in a couple of technical notes from infra onboarding perspective so Jordan/Lina have visibility: 

- Hosted trial onboarding typically takes <1 business day: we provision a tenant, create API keys scoped to the trial, and ingest your evaluation payloads into an isolated namespace. No VPC changes required.
- Dedicated Sandbox provisioning: ~48h after approval. We allocate a temporary GPU pool (4x A100-equivalent by default), pre-deploy the model variant, and run load tests with a shared ingress endpoint. We provide metrics (p50/p95, token cost) and a post-run report.
- VPC trial: dependent on your network team. Requirements we'll need from Lina: CIDR ranges to allowlist, any proxy or egress rules, and KMS key ARN if you want customer-managed keys. Once we have those, engineering lead time is 5–10 business days (can be faster with pre-approved L2 permissions).

I will prepare a short onboarding checklist and a provisioning ETA table for each option and share it by EOD. Also attaching the perf-run checklist in the poc-environment-options.pdf (see tab 3).

If hosted-first is acceptable to you, Rafael can kick off credential creation Monday morning and we can run the initial latency/quality pass Tuesday. If you want to parallelize, we can start network intake for VPC in parallel.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

Attachments: poc-environment-options.pdf
